items.title: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Microsoft researchers dissect the underground infrastructure ecosystem fueling global phishing operations. The report details how threat actors leverage bulletproof hosting, domain generation algorithms, and compromised legitimate services to evade takedowns. IT defenders gain actionable intelligence on infrastructure indicators, hosting patterns, and mitigation strategies to disrupt attacker supply chains before campaigns scale.

items.title: Joint advisory: state-sponsored spear-phishing campaigns targeting ...
items.excerpt: A Five Eyes joint advisory warns of state-sponsored spear-phishing campaigns actively targeting critical national infrastructure across energy, transport, and water sectors. The report outlines TTPs, including highly tailored lures and credential harvesting techniques designed to bypass standard email security. Infrastructure operators are urged to implement enhanced monitoring, restrict external access, and validate authentication anomalies immediately.

items.title: Inside Tycoon2FA: How a leading AiTM phishing kit operated at scale | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Microsoft analyzes the Tycoon2FA kit, a sophisticated Adversary-in-the-Middle platform enabling real-time session hijacking at scale. The breakdown reveals how the kit automates proxying, bypasses MFA, and harvests tokens. Defenders learn to detect proxy traffic patterns, enforce conditional access policies, and deploy browser isolation to neutralize AiTM threats effectively.

items.title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: This investigation traces the EvilTokens campaign, which weaponizes Microsoft’s device code flow to bypass traditional MFA controls. Attackers trick users into entering codes on malicious sites, granting full account access. The article provides detection rules for anomalous device code usage, recommends disabling unnecessary device code flows, and outlines response playbooks for compromised identities.

items.title: Phishing campaign exploits OAuth redirection to bypass defenses
items.excerpt: Researchers uncover campaigns abusing legitimate OAuth protocol redirection to bypass email and web filters. By manipulating callback URLs, attackers route victims to credential harvesting pages while maintaining trusted domain appearances. The analysis highlights the need for strict OAuth scope validation, URL filtering enhancements, and monitoring for unusual authorization requests to protect identity infrastructure.

items.title: Tracking BigBear 2.0 Evilginx2 Phishing Campaign | CloudSEK
items.excerpt: CloudSEK tracks the BigBear 2.0 campaign leveraging Evilginx2 to conduct large-scale AiTM attacks. The report maps the campaign’s infrastructure, phishing templates, and target sectors. IT teams receive guidance on identifying Evilginx2 proxy signatures, blocking associated domains, and implementing certificate pinning to prevent session token theft and lateral movement.

items.title: 500+ Org Phishing Campaign: Critical Infrastructure Risk | Satyam ...
items.excerpt: An analysis of a coordinated phishing wave impacting over 500 organizations in aviation, energy, and logistics. The campaign exploits supply chain trust and uses credential harvesting to pivot into critical systems. Defenders are advised to audit third-party access, enforce strict MFA, monitor for anomalous login patterns, and isolate compromised accounts to prevent infrastructure-wide breaches.

items.title: GhostCode attackers abuse device codes to take over Microsoft 365 accounts
items.excerpt: GhostCode threat actors exploit Microsoft 365 device code authentication to hijack enterprise accounts. The article details how attackers distribute malicious links prompting users to enter verification codes, effectively bypassing MFA. Infrastructure defenders learn to monitor for suspicious device code grants, restrict flow usage via Conditional Access, and deploy user awareness training to mitigate identity takeover risks.

items.title: CVE-2026-53997
items.excerpt: Netherman Portal del Hermano (portaldelhermano.es) before 2026-10-06 contains a broken authentication vulnerability in its password-recovery flow at the POST /password/create-access and POST /password/email endpoints, allowing unauthenticated attackers to take over any member account across all tenants by exploiting the lack of rate limiting and distinct error messages that act as oracles for each of the four identity-verification factors (DNI, date of birth, phone number, last four IBAN digits)

items.title: CVE-2026-63160
items.excerpt: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a vulnerability where the persistent remember-me token is stored verbatim server-side, making the stored value identical to the bearer credential held in the user's cookie. Attackers who gain access to the stored token, such as through database or backup disclosure, can replay the plaintext value to authenticate as the victim user without needing their password.

items.title: CVE-2026-63159
items.excerpt: Omnispace Agora Project before 26.10.0 contains a predictable password-reset token vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to take over user accounts by computing the reset token as sha1(login.password), a deterministic and reusable value. Attackers can derive or brute-force the reset token from known or guessed login and password combinations to forge valid password-reset requests and hijack arbitrary accounts.

items.title: CVE-2026-93909
items.excerpt: IBM WebSphere Application Server - Liberty 17.0.0.3 through 26.0.0.10 is vulnerable by an authentication bypass vulnerability when samlWeb-2.0 feature is enabled.

items.title: CVE-2026-109371
items.excerpt: ZITADEL 3.0.0 before 4.18.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the hosted Login V1 UI, where the change-username handler acts on the account bound to a login flow before any factor is verified. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a victim's login name and then post a new username to rename any active human user, including administrators, locking them out.

items.title: CVE-2026-70580
items.excerpt: Missing authentication for critical function in Windows Credential Guard allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing locally.

items.title: CVE-2026-84313
